title: Transport in a constant type family: for P(x) equal to a fixed B there is a path from the transport of b along p to b

standard_prerequisites: Dependent type families over A and the identity type of A with its reflexivity element.
Transport along a path: for p in x = y a function from P(x) to P(y), with the computation rule that transport along refl x is the identity function by definition.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) with its conversion rule.
core_obligations: Construct, by path induction, for a constant family P(x) = B and every path p in x = y a path in B from the transport of b along p to b.
Name the constructed path the transport of a constant family, written transconst.
proof_roadmap: Fix b in B and define the type family D over x, y, p by D(x, y, p) = (transport of p applied to b equals b).
Base case: D(x, x, refl x) is (transport of refl x applied to b equals b), which is definitionally (b = b) by the computation rule for transporting.
Inhabit the base case by d(x) = refl b and apply path induction to obtain, for every path p, an element of D(x, y, p), as desired.
difficulty_reason: A single path induction with a one-element base case; the only care point is invoking the computation rule for transport along refl in the base case.
